test_title: PYST 68: SSC CGL 2024 - English (Held On 19 Sept, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.

(A) a lot

(B) my daily routine

(C) i have missed

(D) since my retirement

(E) at the workplace
solution:
The correct answer is** Option (1)** i.e. **CBEAD**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **(C)** "I have missed" is the starting part because "I" is the subject and "have missed" is the verb phrase. It tells us what action is happening, which is the missing of something.
 
• **(B) **"my daily routine" comes after (C) because it tells us what the speaker has missed. Without this part, the sentence would be incomplete.
 
• **(E)** "at the workplace" specifies the location where the routine was carried out. This fits logically right after "my daily routine" to clarify the context.
 
• **(A)** "a lot" tells us how much the speaker misses their routine. This phrase is best placed after "I have missed" and before the time frame. It emphasizes the extent of what is being missed.
 
• **(D)** "since my retirement" gives us the time frame or the starting point of when the missing began.

 
 
• **Final Sentence:** "I have missed my daily routine at the workplace a lot since my retirement."

Therefore, the correct answer is **CBEAD****.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2 (**BACED**):** The phrase "a lot" is placed too early, disrupting the logical flow and making the sentence sound unnatural.
 
• **Option 3 (**BEADC**):** The phrase "since my retirement" is misplaced, disrupting the natural flow of the sentence.
 
• **Option 4 (**BADEC**):** "a lot" is incorrectly placed before "my daily routine" and "since my retirement" is out of place.
